name: Crazy Snacks Limited
summary: Regional bakery expansion thesis constrained by cash realization and leverage. FY26 group sales rose 4.4% to ₹116.29 crore but remained below FY24; three-year CAGR is 9.27%. BQS 4.22 and GQS 4.45 reflect mixed-to-weak quality and persistent working-capital demands. At the secondary 19 October close of ₹52, the conditional base model yields 7.12% annualized return. Actual IPO deployment, lender headroom and complete liquidity remain unverified, so IAS is NS. No compounder designation, default allegation or investment instruction.

sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: Crazy Snacks is a regional bakery and packaged-food expansion/value thesis, not an evidence-backed compounder. Fresh bread and bun distribution, together with highly utilized bakery lines, supports an automation opportunity. Yet working capital and debt, rather than demand alone, constrain shareholder outcomes. FY26 group sales were ₹116.29 crore, core EBITDA ₹17.16 crore and CFO ₹4.16 crore, against ₹77.33 crore debt before the July IPO. At the secondary 19 October close of ₹52, conditional bear/base/bull terminal values are ₹0/₹73.33/₹151.40, equivalent to −100%/+7.12%/+23.83% annualized returns without dividends. These are five-year scenarios, not targets: actual IPO deployment and lender availability remain unverified, so IAS is NS. Audit warnings and rating noncooperation are assessed with their counterevidence, not as proof of default or misconduct. [S4][S5][S6][S10]

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: Crazy Snacks Limited, ISIN INE0RBX01014, BSE SME code 544807 and symbol CRAZY. Incorporated in 1995, converted to public status in 2024 and completed its IPO in July 2026. Consolidated Indian GAAP/AS accounts include 99%-owned Crazy Bakery Udyog and wholly owned, inactive Crazyfun Foods. FY26 consolidated statements use ₹ lakh; standalone statements in the same filing use ₹ thousand. This review converts both explicitly and does not mix their scopes. The cutoff is 20 October 2026 UTC, using FY26 results filed on 8 October and a secondary close of ₹52 dated 19 October. Post-IPO shares are 23,937,830 and reference market capitalization ₹124.48 crore. Horizon: five years; analytical equity hurdle: 15% nominal before personal taxes; liquidity reference: ₹5 lakh, not a recommended allocation. G1/G2 are conditional, G3 is held for current funding verification and G4 is conditional. Historical confidence is medium; current funding and liquidity confidence are low. [S4][S5][S6][S10][MX1]

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: Canonical factors are GOV 4, MOAT 5, REV 4, DUR 6, CAP 4, CASH 3, BAL 3, EXEC 4 and EARN 5. BQS is 4.22 and GQS 4.45. Persistent CASH weakness invokes the GQS cap of 5, although the raw score is already below it. R and L remain NS; D and P are 3. The structured audit shows exact original weights, raw arithmetic, missing-data bounds and final values, without redistributing missing weights. A one-point move in GOV changes BQS by 0.20; one point in CAP changes BQS by 0.12 and GQS by 0.15. Such judgment sensitivity exceeds some apparent ranking differences. Quality scores may be compared provisionally, but IAS is not rankable and the conclusion remains a funding hold. [E1–E11]

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: The group manufactures bread, buns, rusk, cakes, cookies and snacks in Gorakhpur and sells mainly through regional distributors. Rusk, bread and buns supplied about 85.9% of FY25 revenue and 87.7% in the nine months to December 2025. Packs priced ₹2–5 contributed 25.85% of FY25 revenue, making packaging and ingredient inflation economically important. The top ten customers accounted for 7.06% of FY25 sales, down from 16.20% in FY23, so geography is a greater concentration risk than one buyer. The detailed business table implies Uttar Pradesh/Bihar shares of 98.40% in FY25 and 94.76% in nine-month FY26. The risk table prints inconsistent 99.16%/99.90%. Both original layouts were checked; either version establishes heavy regional exposure, but exact percentages require correction. Distributor sales are not equivalent to immediate retail cash: receivables and packaging stocks absorb substantial funding. [S4]

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: Freshness, route density and retailer relationships can support delivery-cost and availability advantages in bread and buns. The supporting evidence is nearly full utilization of those lines and a diversified small-customer base. The failure modes are product substitution, promotional spending in new regions and limited ability to pass on commodity costs. No independently verified market share or durable pricing power was established. Anjani Foods is a closer regional bakery/retail comparator, but its stores and leases differ: FY26 group revenue was ₹62.73 crore and CFO ₹2.27 crore. Bikaji is a branded-scale benchmark, with FY26 group revenue ₹2,993.86 crore and CFO ₹304.10 crore, not a multiple to transfer mechanically. Annapurna is relevant to low-ticket regional snacks; the issuer's peer comparison uses FY25 sales of ₹407.97 crore, but an independent current update was not recovered. None of these comparisons supplies a current trading multiple for this model. [S4][S8][S9]

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: FY23–26 consolidated revenues were ₹89.1252/₹127.5932/₹111.3821/₹116.2885 crore. The three-year CAGR is 9.27%, with annual additions of ₹38.4680/−₹16.2111/+₹4.9064 crore. FY26 growth of 4.4% remains a partial recovery below the FY24 peak. A five- or ten-year constant-scope CAGR is ND: the bakery partnership became a company in 2022, so older standalone accounts cannot simply be spliced into this group history. Parent production was 16,033 MT in FY26, versus 14,978 in FY25 and 17,727 in FY24; subsidiary production was 2,346/2,382/2,337 MT. Product volume and mix therefore matter more than headline profit growth. Nine-month revenue of ₹87.5413 crore is not annualized and no unsupported TTM is constructed. REV 4 uses the preselected three-year window; further price/volume decomposition is ND. [S4][S5]

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: Net fresh IPO proceeds of ₹21.8957 crore allocate ₹9.9201 crore to equipment/infrastructure, ₹5.7059 crore to debt prepayment and ₹6.2698 crore to general corporate purposes during FY27. Proposed parent capacity rises from 20,280 to 27,480 MT and group capacity from 25,860 to 33,060 MT. Bread/bun utilization near 99% supports targeted investment, while cakes around 22%, subsidiary chips around 15% and namkeen around 23% warn against assuming uniform demand. Some equipment orders were unplaced at the prospectus date; quotes were not bank-appraised and taxes/freight can add cost. The annual model caps sales by staged capacity, 85% utilization and 2.5% annual realization growth. It explicitly funds maintenance, expansion and working capital and tests delay and a 50% project overrun. The incremental return-on-capital proxy is about 7%, below an analyst 12–16% capital-cost range, but ₹23.20 crore CWIP is immature, so this is not a project IRR. Weak historical cash conversion limits growth quality even if margins improve. [S4][S5][E10][E11]

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text: Promoter experience and loans support operations. December 2025 loans from Navin and Upma totaled about ₹16.57 crore; the related Crazy Bakers advance was about ₹1.02 crore. Subsidiary advances are eliminated on consolidation, not automatically characterized as promoter extraction. FY25 director remuneration was ₹0.42 crore versus ₹0.48 crore in FY24. Counterweights include recurring rating noncooperation, physical-verification limitations and audit-trail weaknesses in the inactive subsidiary. The auditor states that alternative procedures provided sufficient evidence, issued an unmodified opinion and reported no bank default during FY26; this is historical counterevidence, not October funding clearance. The ₹5 crore tax demand concerning share premium is appealed, not a criminal finding; FY26 CARO gives total disputed tax of ₹5.2376 crore. The earlier note's additional ₹5.434 crore contingency needs an updated schedule. The IPO was completed, but FY27 automation commissioning and Crazyfun's intended winding-up remain unverified. A 30 September secretary resignation filing was located; its reason was not independently read or assumed adverse. [S4][S5][S6][S7][S11]

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text: The financial history and calculation fields retain the complete figures. FY26 PBT ₹8.7156 crore plus interest ₹4.4399 and D&A ₹4.0589, less other income ₹0.0584, gives core EBITDA ₹17.1560 crore and a 14.75% margin. EBIT interest coverage is about 2.95x. FY25 prior-period interest subsidy of ₹0.7631 crore is not recurring growth. Prospectus FY25 restated PAT of ₹6.3331 crore differs from the latest statutory comparative ₹6.1126 crore; payroll, other expenses and tax bases differ, and an exact note reconciliation remains open. FY25 gross capex ₹9.1249 crore less disposal proceeds ₹1.4078 crore equals the prospectus net ₹7.7171 crore, not missing cash. FY26 CFO ₹4.1563 crore reflects inventory absorption ₹12.9073 crore, receivable release ₹0.3708 crore, payable funding ₹1.8614 crore and other-liability outflow ₹1.8162 crore. Only ₹0.0104 crore tax was paid against current tax expense ₹2.2517 crore: future cash tax cannot be assumed zero. Capex ₹17.5276 crore leaves FCF proxy −₹13.3713 crore. Net borrowing before finance charges was ₹14.0758 crore. Cumulative FY24–26 CFO/PAT is 52.5%; FY23 transfer effects prevent using that year as a clean organic cash baseline. FY26 inventory ₹35.43 crore, receivables ₹38.93 crore and CWIP ₹23.20 crore tie up capital. Average receivable days rise from about 109.6 to 122.8 despite slightly lower closing receivables. Latest detailed December 2025 aging shows ₹5.57 crore older than six months and ₹1.48 crore older than one year, all considered good. No exact normalized CFO is invented. [S4][S5]

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
Model correction — 20 October 2026: The opening-claim treatment in our earlier scenario calculations was incomplete. This revision explicitly bridges identified current settlements, retained net noncurrent claims and uncertain-composition sensitivities. The updated model replaces the earlier scenario version; the companies’ historical financial figures and published accounts have not changed.

Post-IPO reference owner EPS is ₹2.66 and static P/E about 19.1x at ₹52; the reported pre-IPO weighted EPS ₹3.63 is not the correct current share denominator. March debt/cash cannot be called October EV. The conditional model adds net IPO funds once, assumes the earmarked debt repayment, ring-fences project cash and treats only general-purpose proceeds as free cash. Bear/base/bull cases use annual demand growth 0%/8%/15%, EBITDA margins 10%/14.5%/16%, NWC/sales 68%/58%/50%, debt costs 11%/8.5%/7.5% and exit EV/EBITDA 6x/9x/12x. Capacity limits apply. Annual rows calculate tax, capex, working capital, interest, borrowing, repayment, closing cash/debt and fixed assets. Terminal equity deducts debt and minority claims and adds cash once. Conditional terminal prices are ₹0/₹73.15/₹151.22; the base annualized return is 7.06%, below the 15% hurdle even before execution costs. The audit includes a growth/multiple grid, hurdle ±3 points, trading costs, unavailable cash, tax claims, dilution and project delays/overruns. Multiples are analyst assumptions, not current peer quotes. Actual IPO deployment and credit availability remain material unknowns, so R and IAS stay NS. [S4][S5][S6][S10][E11] New draws incur half-year interest, with ordinary repayments at year-end; tax, interest and borrowing are solved jointly. The reference cases do not settle the unresolved ₹4.4268 crore current-provision balance; this is an incomplete timing assumption, not a zero-liability conclusion. The separate fully funded sensitivity pays the entire balance once in FY27, without asserting that all of it is income tax. Both treatments deduct the reported ₹0.4440 crore noncurrent claim from terminal equity. Reference bear/base/bull prices are ₹0.0000/₹73.1471/₹151.2151, with annual returns -100.0000%/7.0629%/23.7993%. Full-current-provision-settlement prices are ₹0.0000/₹70.7792/₹148.9132, with returns -100.0000%/6.3605%/23.4201%. Normal liabilities already deducted in opening WC are not paid twice.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: The strongest bear argument is that expansion requires distributor credit and inventory faster than profit converts into cash. Input inflation and regional competition compress margins; stocks age, collections slow, project costs remain payable and refinancing becomes expensive. The stress links these effects rather than merely reducing EPS. The severe case assumes 10% annual sales decline, 7% EBITDA margin, 75% NWC/sales, 13% debt cost, a delayed project, unavailable earmarked cash and a ₹10.6716 crore contingency cash charge. This is a scenario, not a claim that all contingencies are payable. Recovery depends on realizable receivables, inventory and plant, not book equity alone. Permanent-loss risk is High, while modeled borrowing remains a requirement rather than a committed facility. Cash realization after commissioning is the decisive thesis variable. [S4][S5][S6][E11] Including half-year interest on new draws, severe-case peak required debt is ₹111.93 crore; terminal common equity remains zero. With the opening-claim convention, the severe case requires peak modeled debt of ₹111.9270 crore, terminal price ₹0.0000 and annual return -100.0000%. These are conditional funding requirements, not evidence of committed facilities. Paying the whole unresolved current provision increases severe peak debt to ₹119.8965 crore. That bound is separate from any contingent disputed-tax stress already modeled.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: At ₹52, fivefold and tenfold prices would be ₹260 and ₹520, implying equity values around ₹622 crore and ₹1,245 crore before new dilution. Proposed capacity of 33,060 MT at 85% utilization and five years of 2.5% realization growth supports roughly ₹201 crore sales. Even 16% EBITDA margin and 12x EV/EBITDA would imply only about ₹386 crore enterprise value before debt, below the fivefold equity requirement. Thus a fivefold five-year outcome is unsupported by the funded capacity plan alone. It would require more capacity and capital, stronger distribution/unit economics or a materially higher multiple. Tenfold is still more demanding. No precise success probability is assigned. [S4][E11]

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Monitor: (1) ₹9.9201 crore equipment deployment and 7,200 MT added capacity, with FY27 delay or unfunded overrun triggering reassessment. (2) ₹5.7059 crore debt prepayment and remaining IPO balances; unexplained use or shortfall is critical. (3) Cash conversion versus the 52.5% three-year baseline: seek over 80% with actual taxes paid; another negative CFO year despite profit is a warning. (4) Receivables ₹38.93 crore and aging: worsening old balances without collections require provisions/valuation review. (5) Inventory ₹35.43 crore: obtain physical-count and packaging-aging reconciliation; a material unexplained shortage would break the thesis. (6) Lender cooperation, limits and payments: a missed obligation escalates G3. (7) ₹5.2376 crore tax appeal and other contingencies: incorporate orders and cash settlements, not presumed guilt. (8) Sales versus the ₹127.59 crore FY24 peak and added output: judge collections, not distributor counts alone. (9) Complete BSE turnover, lots, restrictions and order-book depth before implementation. Review on new filings; no monitoring automation was created. [S4][S5][S6][S10]

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Hold — unresolved current funding and liquidity. This is a working-capital-intensive expansion thesis with mixed-to-weak demonstrated quality, not a compounder. Deep status means applicable research and a conditional funded annual/equity model were completed; it does not mean all public-data uncertainties disappeared. P/E alone does not establish inexpensive cash-generative FMCG economics. Supported quality factors remain visible, but IAS cannot be ranked. Verified post-IPO cash/debt, collections, commissioning and complete execution data could unlock a supported return assessment. No trade, allocation or portfolio-exit instruction follows. [S4][S5][S6][S10]

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: The ledger distinguishes the issuer-linked final prospectus dated 30 June, the original 8 October results filing mirrored by FinancialReports, primary CRISIL rationales, peer annual reports and secondary dated market data. The earlier PDF font problem was resolved and is not an issuer financial defect. Remaining questions are complete FY26 notes, the exact FY25 restatement, IPO deployment and cash restrictions, current maturities/lender headroom, physical-count clarification, tax/other claim status and full BSE trading coverage. Geographic drafting inconsistencies are documented and bounded, not automatically treated as a critical G2 failure. Future margins, tax, financing costs, capacity realization, timing and terminal multiples are analyst assumptions. No authorized borrowing ceiling is relabeled as a committed bank facility, and no management forecast is treated as an achieved result. [S4–S11] The opening-claim reconciliation distinguishes current cash settlements, normal operating liabilities already in working capital, net noncurrent employee/deposit claims retained at exit, and uncertain composition bounds. March balances are not asserted to remain outstanding in October. No immediate payment of all noncurrent provisions is assumed.

valuation.formulas: EBITDA=revenue×margin; tax=max(EBIT−interest including half-year new draws,0)×25%; FCF=EBITDA−interest−tax−ΔNWC−projectcapex−maintenance. Release earmarkedIPOcash only againstproject. Borrow to₹1crcashfloor; repay debt with excess. EV=terminalEBITDA×multiple; equity=max(EV−debt+cash−NCI,0); price=equity×1e7/shares; IRR=(terminalprice/52)^.2−1. No dividends and cash counted once. New borrowing incurs half-year interest in the year drawn. Ordinary excess-cash repayments occur at year-end and receive no same-year interest saving. Curis collateral-funded FD overdraft repayment retains its explicit half-year timing. Interest, positive-profit cash tax and funding draw are solved jointly to a 1e-12 crore tolerance; new borrowing is a funding requirement, not a committed facility. Opening-claim extension: first-year operating cash deducts identified excluded current tax/employee/expense claims once. Approved post-anchor dividends are separate financing cash outflows, with no buyer entitlement added. Terminal equity=max(0,original operating enterprise/equity bridge before its zero floor - retained net noncurrent claim). Normal WC liabilities are already captured and are not charged twice. The full-current-provision bound, where shown, replaces the unresolved zero-settlement reference rather than adding another copy of that liability.

reverse_expectations.interpretation: Read required terminal enterprise value against funded operating path, rather than solving an unconstrained CAGR beyond physicalcapacity.

valuation.opening_provision_reference_treatment: Reference cases retain the unresolved zero-settlement timing assumption for current provisions of 4.4268 crore, not a zero-liability assertion. The separate full-settlement scenario pays the entire balance in FY27. All cases deduct the separately reported noncurrent claim at terminal equity. Composition and actual timing remain unavailable.
valuation.opening_claim_convention: Known current exclusions paid once in FY27; opening net noncurrent deficits/deposit liabilities retained at unchanged nominal amount in terminal equity. Future modeled compensation and operating expenses are treated as cash funded, so no unsupported future deficit build-up is added. This is a conditional steady-deficit convention, not a claim of immediate legal maturity. Normal opening WC liabilities are not charged twice.

valuation.model_correction_notice: Model correction — 20 October 2026: The opening-claim treatment in our earlier scenario calculations was incomplete. This revision explicitly bridges identified current settlements, retained net noncurrent claims and uncertain-composition sensitivities. The updated model replaces the earlier scenario version; the companies’ historical financial figures and published accounts have not changed.

GOV.reason: Recurring information-cooperation lapses and cash/inventory verification limitations weaken stewardship confidence; large promoter loans support funding and modest remuneration are counterevidence. No substantiated diversion or minority abuse established.

MOAT.reason: Dense regional bakery distribution and near-full bread/bun lines support freshness/service economics; top10 customer share only7.06% reduces single-buyer dependence. Subscale snacks lines, geographic concentration and larger branded competitors constrain pricing and durable excess returns.

REV.reason: Three-year FY23–26 comparable reported group CAGR9.27% earns4. Five-year constant-scope history unavailable after partnership-to-company transition. FY25 decline and FY26 rebound remain belowFY24 peak; no discretionary adjustment. Growth is not inferred from margin expansion.

DUR.reason: Bread/bun demand and7200MT funded equipment plan offer accessible local runway; existing bread/bun utilization near99% supports targeted capacity. Regional concentration, weakly utilized chips/namkeen and uncertain new-state economics limit the runway score.

CAP.reason: FY23–26 incremental capital-return proxy about7% is below analyst12–16% capital-cost range, while debt/CWIP expanded ahead of sales. New assets are not fully mature, so this is mixed/weak demonstrated economics rather than proof of permanently destructive projectIRRs.

CASH.reason: FY24–26 cumulative CFO/PAT about52.5%; FY25 negativeCFO followed by FY26inventory absorption12.9073cr and almost no current cash tax. PositiveFY24/FY26cash and stableFY26receivables are counterevidence but do not erase persistent collection/inventory funding demands. Persistent cash override applies.

BAL.reason: PreIPO debt77.33cr versus17.16cr coreEBITDA and only0.759cr cash; materialtaxclaim and weakly confirmed lender access. NetIPO21.90cr and promoter support help, but only5.71cr earmarkeddebtrepayment and no verifiedOctober liquiditybridge. Conditional funding risk, not evidenced default.

EXEC.reason: FY26 revenue still belowFY24 despite greater investedcapital; bread/bunlines almostfull but snack utilization low and cash conversion weak. FY26bread/rusk volumeimprovement and completedIPO are positive; FY27automation commissioning not yetverified. No invented missed formal revenueguidance.

EARN.reason: FY26 coreEBITDA17.156cr and lowotherincome support operatingprofit; priorinterestsubsidy0.7631cr and FY24discountincome require normalization. OwnerPAT6.5039cr divided bypostIPOshares gives₹2.72 versusreportedpreIPOweighted₹3.63, so profitgrowth is not equivalent to persharegrowth.

R.reason: Conditional model is fully linked, but actual postIPOcash/debt and current creditheadroom unverified; do not convert contingent returns into a supported R.

D.reason: Funded stress links marginloss, slowerNWC, delayedcapex and claims to debt/lowequityrecovery. IPOrelief is partial and no blanketdefault claim; significant impairment risk at₹52.

P.reason: StaticpostIPOPEabout19.1x sits against sub10%historicalgroupgrowth and weakcashconversion. Basefundedgrowth does not automatically earn15%; reverseexitmultiple and sensitivity expose limited room for error, although successfulcashrelease would help.

L.reason: Only38observations in60-sessioncomparisonwindow; observed-only5%exit22.77days already slow. Missingdates not automaticallyzero and BSErestrictions/depth unverified, so formalL remainsNS instead of a falsely exact score.

gates.reason: Control and disclosure weaknesses, tax appeals and noncooperation merit monitoring; no substantiated diversion or minority-abuse finding. Unmodified audit and no reportedFY26bankdefault are counterevidence, not guarantees.

Auditor describes sufficient alternative procedures despite nonphysicalverification. No automaticcriticalhold solely from KAM. DetailedFY26notes, inventorycontrol clarification and smallFY25restatement bridge remain gaps; use reportedvalues with scopeandnormalization cautions.

ActualIPOdeployment and October cash/debt/lenderheadroom remain unverified after issuer-not-cooperating rating. Scenarios explicitly compute borrowingneeds; no evidenceddefault or automaticG3fail imposed.
